name: goap_packaged_loop_arbitrary_target_fixed
supersedes: spec_library/synthesized_registry/goap_packaged_loop_arbitrary_target.meta.json (CORRECTED there, not deleted -- kept as an honest record of the overclaim and how it was caught)
mechanism: Fixes the false-positive gap found when testing target_goal-precondition binding against a genuinely different (non-linear, 'doubling') domain: the packaged action now requires an ADDITIONAL precondition, reaches(X,Target), which is computed via a real, generic transitive-closure/BFS algorithm (reach_closure, in the experiment driver) over the base chain relation -- not authored per-target. The shortcut action can then ONLY fire when Target is genuinely reachable from X via the real primitive chain.
given_background: reach_closure(edges, nodes) is a standard graph-reachability algorithm (BFS from every node) -- generic infrastructure, same status as pred1/succ chains elsewhere, not a solution to any specific reachability question.
verification: Reachable case (1->16 via doubling: 1,2,4,8,16) still solved in a single step. Genuinely UNREACHABLE case (1->6, not a power-of-2-scaled value) now correctly returns an EMPTY plan (no false positive) -- this is the exact negative case that exposed the original flaw.
why_the_original_entry_overclaimed: increment_to_target/decrement_to_target (linear +1/-1 chains) happened to never produce a false positive because EVERY intermediate value is reachable on a linear chain -- so the missing reachability check was invisible until tested against a domain (doubling) where not every target is reachable. The lesson: a packaged action's precondition set must be tested against at least one domain where the 'always trivially true' shape of the precondition would be exposed by a genuine negative case, not just domains where success is guaranteed by construction.
provenance: direct response to: 'OK so... using this approach, let's test that it works across a range of synthesis tasks?' -- the range-testing itself (specifically the non-linear doubling task) is what surfaced the flaw; without deliberately varying the domain shape, the original overclaim would have stood uncaught.
